speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: Quillen’s finite-field calculation: plus construction and Adams operations
summary: Kazhdan explains the proof of the finite-field calculation announced by Gelfand in record 258. The argument passes from a classifying space through a homology-preserving modification to a homotopy fibre of an Adams operation, using Brauer lifting and an étale comparison. Fuchs interrupts on P000424; Kazhdan resumes on P000425. The catalogue's P000423--P000425 interval starts too early and omits the proof's final page. Several apparent finite-rank statements actually require stabilization; the asserted identification of a fixed subgroup with maps into a homotopy fibre is a substantive error. These constructions had already been announced by Quillen at the 1970 ICM, printed in 1971; the later Annals date must not be mistaken for their first circulation.

speaker: D. B. Fuchs
title: When abelianizing the fundamental group preserves integral homology
summary: Fuchs inserts an existence theorem into Kazhdan's discussion: the commutator subgroup must be relatively perfect. He distinguishes existence from uniqueness and then invokes simple spaces and Whitehead's theorem. All of the identifiable intervention is on P000424, not throughout the catalogue's P000423--P000427 range.

speaker: M. Sh. Birman
title: Trace-class perturbations and Gelfand’s spectral classification question
summary: Birman begins a stationary proof of the Kato--Rosenblum theorem and identifies two boundary-value facts used in it. Gelfand asks which prescribed spectral types can be realized with a trace-class difference, and what the spectrum in the corresponding operator quotient means. The next dated heading, Kazhdan on 27 March, begins at the bottom of this same page.

speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: Artin–Mazur étale homotopy and arithmetic symmetry
summary: Kazhdan outlines an algebraic construction of the homotopy type of a variety, its comparison over the complex numbers, and the action of field automorphisms. The completion paragraph runs onto P000428. The ordinary-space terminology in the notes suppresses the pro-homotopy category essential to Artin--Mazur's formulation.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: A reading plan for the seminar’s common categorical language
summary: Gelfand asks participants to learn categories and functors from the first chapter of Grothendieck's Tohoku paper, then topoi and descent from the material accompanying Mumford. This is a reading plan, with no separately stated theorem. It precedes Birman's continuation on the page, although its catalogue record number is later. The plan connects the earlier site and sheaf discussions (for example 1967-143 and 1970-226) to Geronimus's April lectures.

speaker: M. Sh. Birman
title: Stationary and time-dependent wave operators
summary: Birman continues the trace-class scattering proof, explains completeness through reverse wave operators and the chain rule, and derives a resolvent identity controlling spectral densities. He explicitly refers to the 1967 Izvestiya paper. A final sketch gestures toward locally trace-class perturbations and unbounded operators; its missing domain hypotheses are retained as a limitation.

speaker: A. Yu. Geronimus
title: Sites, sheaves, derived cohomology and the classifying topos
summary: Following a minimum reading programme on topology, descent and simplicial methods, Geronimus develops covering families, sheaves, adjunction, derived cohomology and a Leray spectral sequence. He then constructs a classifying site for group objects and applies the language to Quillen's finite-field cohomology calculation. An exercise refers broadly to Artin on formal and algebraic objects, without stating a theorem. The exposition revisits exact earlier occurrences such as 1967-143.2, 1967-143.5 and 1970-226.2--3; no new problem identifier is created for those definitions.

speaker: A. Yu. Geronimus
title: The homotopy category and localization at quasi-isomorphisms
summary: Geronimus builds the derived category from complexes and homotopies, emphasizes its universal property, and explicitly rejects identifying maps merely because they induce the same map on cohomology. A roof construction follows, although the notebook mistakenly calls the resulting limit projective. The examples begin in nonnegative degrees. A crossed-out reprise on P000439 belongs to this discussion but adds no distinct live assertion.

speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: Computing the derived category with injective complexes
summary: Kazhdan supplies the practical model omitted from the preceding abstract localization: enough injectives allow one to work with injective complexes. The adjacent complex-bordism lecture starts only after this short intervention. The omitted boundedness qualification is recoverable from Geronimus's nonnegative complexes on P000437.

speaker: Jack Morava
title: Complex bordism, formal groups and the emerging height picture
summary: Morava starts from geometric bordism and interprets the complex-bordism module of a space as a sheaf on the scheme of formal group laws. Coordinate changes, height strata, periodic theories and division-algebra stabilizers give an early form of chromatic geometry. Lazard and Quillen supply the older foundations; Morava's geometric programme is contemporary research, with a November 1972 unpublished announcement and later published developments. The strong claim that every fibre in one dense open set is integral \(K\)-theory requires substantial repair.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Dyson’s missed opportunities: eta identities and contractions
summary: Gelfand reports two examples from Dyson's Gibbs Lecture of 17 January 1972: the relation between powers of the Dedekind eta function and root systems, and contractions of kinematical groups. The manuscript preserves the explicit five-variable formula for Ramanujan's tau function and singles out the exponent 26 as unexplained. The missing leading factor in the eta product is a mathematical emendation, while the exceptional exponent has a documented later explanation. The final contraction remark occupies only the top of P000446, before Morava's heading.

speaker: Jack Morava
title: Formal groups, invariant differentials and homogeneous orbits
summary: Kirillov first recapitulates the geometric bordism construction and the picture of a bordism module over the coefficient scheme. The discussion then clarifies geometric fibres, coordinate changes, characteristic-zero logarithms and Mishchenko's projective-space coefficients. It ends with a compressed homogeneous-space assertion. The last conclusion is at the top of P000449; P000450--P000451 belong to Gabrielov's 25 September 1972 lecture, outside this record.

title: Catalogue heading: 1972
summary: The catalogue marks the start of a new year. No mathematical assertion belongs to this heading. P000449 ends Morava's 14 April 1972 discussion; P000450 begins Gabrielov's 25 September 1972 lecture, continued on P000451. These adjacent pages explain the supplied overlapping range but do not turn Gabrielov's talk into record 271.

title: Catalogue heading: YEAR 1973
summary: This catalogue heading separates calendar-year material and carries no mathematical talk. P000477 is the end of Buchstaber's 20 November 1972 discussion of formal groups; P000478--P000479 belong to Buchstaber on 12 February 1973. The heading's supplied page range includes both sides of that boundary. Neither adjoining lecture is assigned mathematical occurrences under record 286.

speaker: R. L. Dobrushin
title: Nelson’s Euclidean Markov-field construction
summary: The manuscript explicitly dates this short record 19 February 1973, although the catalogue supplied with the task says 19 February 1972. The YEAR1973 heading and adjacent Buchstaber dates support a catalogue typo. It is retained among the 45 requested records but uses the corrected academic-year prefix 1972. Gelfand distinguishes quantizing given equations from finding physically adequate equations; Dobrushin then identifies Nelson's probabilistic Euclidean-field method and says that Glimm--Jaffe results can ``almost'' be recovered. Only P000480 belongs to this talk: P000479 and P000481 are parts of different Buchstaber lectures.
